glossary.def: A partition of capacity into pools so that a fault or heavy consumer in one pool cannot exhaust capacity for the others.
A client-supplied token that lets a server recognise a repeated request and apply its side effect only once, which makes retries safe.
A rate-limit model where tokens refill at a steady rate and each request spends tokens. It allows bursts up to the bucket size and then limits the sustained rate.
The first request that stores a prompt prefix in a provider cache. On GPT-5.6 and later and on Anthropic it is billed above the normal input rate (1.25x for the short lifetime).
The load figure in the PTU sizing formula: prompt tokens after caching plus output tokens weighted by the output-to-input ratio, summed over peak requests per minute.
A service level indicator is a measured signal such as TTFT p95 or success rate. A service level objective is the target for it, and the allowed miss rate is the error budget.
Deliberately rejecting or degrading low-priority work when capacity is exhausted so that important work keeps succeeding.
A separate quota that caps the input tokens waiting in a Batch queue, so batch work does not disturb online deployments.
A prompt cache with no entries for your prefix, as in a freshly used failover region. The first requests pay full input prices and higher time to first token.

claims.text: On OpenAI GPT-5.6 and later a cache write costs 1.25x the uncached input rate and a cache read 0.1x (0.05x on GPT-6.1 Sol); one write plus nine reads costs 2.15x versus 10x uncached.
OpenAI bills each token at exactly one of the uncached, cached or write rates.
Anthropic prices a 5-minute cache write at 1.25x, a 1-hour write at 2x and a read at 0.1x of base input.

Azure reports reasoning tokens in completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens (Chat Completions) or output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens (Responses) and bills them as output tokens, so hidden reasoning adds to generated tokens.
OpenAI heuristic: cutting 50% of output tokens may cut about 50% of latency, while cutting 50% of the prompt may give only 1% to 5%.
With a 1.25x write and 0.1x read, caching breaks even at the second request inside the lifetime (1.25 + 0.1(N-1) versus N); Anthropic's 2x 1-hour write needs three requests.

APIM semantic cache policies llm-semantic-cache-lookup and llm-semantic-cache-store are paired; score-threshold lower is stricter; Microsoft suggests starting near 0.05 and warns above 0.2 may mismatch and that results can be incorrect, outdated or unsafe.
FrugalGPT reported a cascade matching the best single LLM with up to 98% cost reduction, or beating GPT-4 by 4% at equal cost (2023 benchmarks).
RouteLLM trained routers on preference data and cut cost by more than 2x in some cases with no quality loss.
LLMLingua achieves up to 20x prompt compression with little loss on the tested benchmarks.

Azure model router modes are Balanced (default, within about 1% to 2% of best quality), Cost (about 5% to 6%) and Quality; version 2025-11-18 updates in place; 2025-08-07 and 2025-05-19 are frozen; Global Standard and Data Zone Standard only; context window equals the smallest underlying model; routing reads text only.

Azure quota is TPM per subscription, region, model and deployment type; RPM is 6 per 1,000 TPM for older chat models and 1 per 1,000 TPM for o3 and o4-mini; headers include x-ratelimit-limit-tokens and 429 adds retry-after-ms.
Azure's 429 table lists rate limit exceeded, system capacity throttling and a temporary rate-limit adjustment on Standard, plus a fourth row for max_tokens estimates that inflate counted tokens.
Azure's TPM check counts prompt plus max_tokens plus best_of, and RPM is enforced over 1 or 10 second windows.
Anthropic OTPM counts actual output only, cache reads do not count toward ITPM for most models, and acceleration limits apply to sharp ramps.

Foundry deployment types include GlobalStandard, DataZoneStandard, Standard, GlobalProvisionedManaged, DataZoneProvisionedManaged, ProvisionedManaged, GlobalBatch, DataZoneBatch and DeveloperTier; Microsoft advises starting with Global Standard.
With Global Standard and Data Zone Standard, if the primary region has an interruption, all traffic initially routed to it is affected.
PTU capacity is held whether or not requests arrive; quota and reservations do not guarantee capacity; cached tokens do not consume PTU capacity.
PTU-M deployments keep prompt caching but do not support prompt cache breakpoints or expose cache_write_tokens.
PTU sizing example: 1,000 RPM, 200-token prompt, 20-token response, ratio 8, 3,400 input TPM per PTU, increment 5 gives 105.88 so 110 PTUs, and 80 PTUs at a 50% cache rate.
Spillover sends non-200 overflow from a PTU deployment to a standard deployment in the same resource, per request via x-ms-spillover-deployment, and is not supported for Azure DeepSeek or Meta Llama.
Priority processing sets service_tier priority per deployment or request, with a p50 token-rate target per 5-minute window, not a per-request guarantee.
Azure Global Batch and Data Zone Batch are 50% cheaper than Global Standard, target 24 hours, use a separate enqueued token quota and have no real-time SLA.
OpenAI Batch API: 50% discount, jsonl input with a unique custom_id per request, one model per file, 200 MB upload limit, and output line order may not match input order.
Anthropic Message Batches take up to 100,000 requests or 256 MB, most finish within 1 hour, expire after 24 hours and results are kept 29 days.

Azure Flex processing is preview, set by service_tier flex, 50% discount, no SLA, preemptible, shares quota with Standard, has no automatic fallback to Standard, and from 2026-09-25 unsupported models return 400.
OpenAI Flex is in beta, priced at Batch API rates with prompt caching discounts, and its example raises the client timeout to 15 minutes.
llm-token-limit returns 429 when the rate is exceeded and 403 when the quota is exceeded; counters are per gateway; streaming always estimates; images count up to 1,200 tokens each when estimating.
llm-emit-token-metric allows 5 custom dimensions per policy, 100 unique values per dimension and 1,000 active time series per namespace before data is silently dropped.

An APIM backend has one circuitBreaker rule (failureCondition, tripDuration, acceptRetryAfter), returns 503 when tripped, is approximate across instances and is not in the Consumption tier; pools hold up to 30 backends.
OpenAI advises treating Retry-After as a minimum plus jitter, capping attempts and time, and never retrying quota or billing errors.
Three retries at each of five stacked layers multiply to 243 times the load on the bottom service; retry at a single point in the stack.
A circuit breaker has closed, open and half-open states; half-open lets a limited number of probe requests through.
In a Google BigTable benchmark, hedged requests cut the 99.9th percentile for 1,000 keys from 1,800 ms to 74 ms for about 2% extra requests (via a search summary, PDF not parsed).
Azure's reliability guidance calls for automated detection of degraded components and a notification to users about reduced functionality.
Foundry provides no automatic failover; hot/hot has RTO of minutes and RPO near zero, hot/warm 30 minutes to 2 hours, hot/cold 2 to 8 hours.
An SLO of 99.9% over 30 days leaves 43.2 minutes of error budget (derived arithmetic).
